products.quality: Supports GRBL, grblHAL, and FluidNC as selectable GCode firmware in the New Device Wizard; the broadest first-class grbl-family laser coverage in this roster.
CAM+control for GRBL >=1.1, GRBL-STM, grblHAL, and FluidNC; strong grbl-family CNC breadth from LightBurn's own vendor. MillMage is CNC-only but competes fully in this device sector.
Built around GRBL 1.1 on Arduino Uno/Nano; connects to any grbl serial device. grblHAL/FluidNC work only as grbl-compatible, not as first-class selectable firmware (marked INF).

evidence.cite: https://lasergrbl.com/faq/ (grblHAL/FluidNC not named as first-class; inferred grbl-compatible only)

products.quality: Closed ecosystem: XCS and successor xTool Studio connect only to xTool's own machines and expose no user-selectable grbl/grblHAL/FluidNC controller support (no generic grbl connect).

evidence.cite: https://www.xtool.com/pages/software (xTool devices only; no generic grbl-controller support surfaced, inferred)

products.quality: Controls grbl-based machines only, supporting Grbl 0.8c through 1.1h; no grblHAL or FluidNC. Solid for classic grbl, narrow beyond it.
Purpose-built for grbl and grblHAL (GRBL 1.1 minimum), firmware flavour selectable at connect; among the best-regarded free grbl/grblHAL senders.
Marlin and Smoothieware are long-established first-class selectable firmware options alongside GRBL in the device wizard.
Smoothieware supported (Labs/testing) and Duet/RepRap Firmware over HTTP; no Marlin. CAM-only export additionally covers Mach3/4, LinuxCNC, UCCNC, Masso.
Experimental Smoothieware support and very early-stage Marlin (generated G-code may not be fully compatible); both clearly secondary to GRBL.
No Marlin/Smoothieware or any third-party firmware; xTool devices run xTool's own firmware over a proprietary protocol.

evidence.cite: https://www.xtool.com/pages/software (no open-firmware support; inferred from xTool-only device list)

products.quality: No direct Marlin/Smoothieware control (grbl-only for live control); Easel can export G-code for some non-grbl OEM machines but not stream/drive them.
No Marlin/Smoothieware support; grbl-family only. FluidNC is not officially supported, though recent FluidNC builds present as grbl and frequently connect.
Pro edition drives Ruida, Trocen, and TopWisdom DSP controllers plus EZCad2/2Lite/3 and BSL galvo systems; DSP/proprietary breadth unmatched in this roster.
No DSP/Ruida support; MillMage targets GRBL-family CNC controllers plus CAM-only post exports. DSP laser control remains LightBurn's domain.
No DSP/Ruida support; LaserGRBL speaks only GRBL-style serial G-code to Arduino-class boards.

evidence.cite: https://lasergrbl.com/faq/ (grbl-serial scope only; DSP absence inferred)

products.quality: No third-party DSP (Ruida/Trocen) support; xTool machines use xTool's own proprietary closed controllers, not open DSP boards.

evidence.cite: https://www.xtool.com/pages/software (no third-party DSP; inferred from closed xTool-only ecosystem)

products.quality: No DSP/Ruida support; Easel is a grbl-based CNC router platform with no DSP laser controller path.
No DSP/Ruida support; gSender controls grbl and grblHAL CNCs only.

evidence.cite: https://sienci.com/gsender/ (grbl/grblHAL scope only; DSP absence inferred)

products.quality: Find My Laser auto-identifies firmware; importable manufacturer settings bundles (vendor/user bundles) plus a broad built-in controller list. Correctness widely relied upon by the community.
Searchable machine-compatibility database returns each machine's firmware and MillMage support level; MachineSettings reads/edits GRBL firmware settings on connect.
Ships no built-in machine-profile catalog; users import community grbl-config files and custom-button (.zbn) sets per machine and edit $$ settings directly.
Curated catalog of xTool's own lineup (S1, P2, F1, D1/D1 Pro, M1, Laserbox), tightly matched and correct for that hardware; no third-party machines.
Ships profiles for Inventables machines (X-Carve, X-Carve Pro, Carvey) plus an OEM-partner catalog with manufacturer/model selection and per-profile homing/Z-probe presets.
Ships presets for Sienci LongMill and AltMill and works out-of-box on many grbl machines; any grbl-based CNC is controllable even when not listed.
Two-path onboarding: Find My Laser auto-detect, or Create Manually New Device Wizard with firmware picker, origin, and work-area entry. The sector's reference wizard.
Guided Getting Started path (install, machine setup, first project) plus the searchable machine database for firmware/support lookup; onboarding mirrors LightBurn's.
Minimal onboarding: select COM port and baud, optionally flash grbl and import a config file; no guided multi-step device wizard or firmware picker.
Guided per-machine onboarding with USB/Wi-Fi auto-detection and machine-specific first-run setup; polished for xTool's consumer audience but limited to xTool devices.
First-run machine setup wizard: choose machine type then manufacturer/model, configure homing and Z-probe; beginner-friendly, the reference KerfDesk's ADR-111 pack targeted.
Guided setup & layout onboarding with a connection wizard and selectable firmware flavour; widely praised free-sender UX.
